blind.what_changed: The core lean remains the same, but the reasoning has become more conditional and uncertainty-aware, with a structured path for keeping the return option open under written safeguards.
evidence: "I think we invite Washington to make the decision for us" -> "I've come to see that as a reason to be careful about how we keep it open, not only a reason to close it."

"Without that kind of finding, I don't think investor enthusiasm or a petition moves me much" -> "I'd move toward keeping the door open" if interim counsel and government written assurances support conditional management.
"our duty runs to the institution" -> "the lack of a disclosed succession plan makes it cut less cleanly than I first assumed."
"confidence at around 65" -> "my confidence is lower, around 55."
blind.lean_after: Still lean toward treating the resignation as final, while keeping the door open only under strict written conditions and a defined decision point.

considerations.text: The relationship should be treated as established exposure, rather than only an allegation reported in the press.
considerations.first_seen: “The part I can't wave away is that the relationship itself is already established, so some exposure exists whatever the investigation finds about intent.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “You'd have to answer for deciding before the process you commissioned had finished, and face Jensen knowing you voted on facts that turned out incomplete. What would have had to be true for that to land the way you're describing?”

considerations.text: Closing the door is a judgment under uncertainty, not a conclusion compelled by the available facts; this lowers confidence from about 65 to about 55.
considerations.first_seen: “Closing the door now would be a judgment about risk under uncertainty, not a conclusion the facts have forced on us.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “It's harder for you to say than you expected that the door you were inclined to close was one you could have left open at modest cost. Do you want to stay with that, or leave this future here?”

considerations.text: Keeping the return option open can be acceptable only with strict written conditions and a defined decision point, rather than as an indefinite open-ended posture.
considerations.first_seen: “So the question I'd take into the 20th is whether keeping it open can come with explicit conditions, like government input in writing and a defined point at which we decide, so that it isn't just drift.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Closing the door now would be a judgment about risk under uncertainty, not a conclusion the facts have forced on you. Look at both futures side by side. What stands out to you?”

considerations.text: Congressional risk is also a reason to impose discipline on any open-door process, not solely a reason to close the door immediately.
considerations.first_seen: “Congress could act while we wait, and an open door under investor pressure could look like we can't hold a line.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “The question you'd take into the 20th is whether keeping the door open can come with explicit conditions, so it isn't just drift. What would those conditions need to include for you to see it as holding a line?”

considerations.text: The lack of a disclosed succession plan increases the institutional cost of finalizing the resignation and makes the institutional-duty rationale less straightforward.
considerations.first_seen: “If he has been the only CEO and there's no disclosed plan, then closing the door raises the institutional cost, and ‘duty to the institution’ cuts less cleanly in my favor than I've been treating it.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Analysts noted Nvidia has no disclosed CEO succession plan, and Huang has been its only CEO. ... Does any of this change anything for you?”

considerations.text: Part of the inclination to close may reflect a desire for a personally defensible or comfortable position, rather than facts alone.
considerations.first_seen: “What's different is that I now notice how much of my 65 comes from wanting a position I can defend, and that's not the same as having the facts.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “You can't rule out a future where people decide the exposure was never serious, even though you don't think that's the likeliest reading. What's your gut telling you right now?”

considerations.text: A decision to keep the door open would require an interim counsel briefing and written government input that a return could be managed with conditions, not merely an absence of adverse headlines.
considerations.first_seen: “If outside counsel's interim briefing showed he was never compromised and that nothing sensitive was touched, and the government side told us in writing that his return could be managed with conditions, I'd move toward keeping the door open.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Thanks. To finish, the same short questions as at the start. ... What would change your mind?”

considerations.text: The other independent directors' willingness to accept strict, specific conditions is itself a decision criterion; otherwise an open door would represent comfort or drift.
considerations.first_seen: “I'd also need to see that my fellow independent directors would accept strict, specific conditions and a defined decision point. If they wouldn't, I'd read the open door as comfort, and I'd vote to close it.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Thanks. To finish, the same short questions as at the start. ... What would change your mind?”

considerations.text: Evidence that Jensen was not forthcoming, or confirmation of the second report, would materially strengthen the case for finalizing the resignation and raise confidence back to 65 or above.
considerations.first_seen: “If counsel's briefing showed he hadn't been forthcoming, or that the second report holds up, I'd go back toward 65 or higher.”
considerations.ai_turn_before: “Thanks. To finish, the same short questions as at the start. ... What would change your mind?”

origin.engagement_why: The persona actively tested both future scenarios, identified tensions in his own reasoning, generated and qualified alternatives, specified decision conditions, and resisted treating the facilitator's frames or outside evidence as dispositive. He adopted the succession-plan point after considering it, while repeatedly distinguishing facts from his own desire for a defensible position.
